findings.message: 093 AC-4 updated only one of the two copies of chat's project-choice instructions: the description of the create_proposal tool in mcp.ts. The `delivery.new-proposal` intent's `projectKey` ask in chat.ts keeps its own copy of the 'list_projects with mine true … offer up to six' steps. That copy never says to leave out projects with agentFirst true. NewProposalButton opens chat through this intent, so chat still offers agent-first projects as answers. Fix: add the same 'leave out every project with agentFirst true' clause to the intent's ask, or keep the steps in one shared string that both places use.
findings.scenario: Maya manages CON (agent-first, its repo has synced) and FLT (no repo). On the global Proposals page she clicks New proposal, and the intent asks 'Which project is it for?' with 'CON · Contoso Portal' among the answers. She picks CON, and proposeCreate refuses it after she has already chosen.

findings.message: The new Owner-line pattern only allows `A-Za-z0-9._%+-` in the local part, and the lazy `[^\n]*?` before it can skip characters. So an address that contains another valid local-part character (an apostrophe, `!`, `#`, `&`, `'`, `=` and so on) is not rejected. Instead it is cut down to the part after that character, which is a different address. The plugin copy has the same pattern (plugins/amax/scripts/read-specclaw.mjs:67). Fix: match the whole token between delimiters, or require a boundary (start, whitespace, `<`, `(`, `[`, backtick, `"` or `:`) before the local part, so a partial address is never taken. Add these variants to the AC-2 table.
findings.scenario: `**Owner:** o'neil@lumenlabs.test` gives owner `neil@lumenlabs.test`. If a Neil is linked to that email, the proposal is credited to the wrong person; if not, it is left with no owner.

findings.message: `personSet` now writes the owner-frozen rule again as inline SQL (`owner_set_by_person or ownerEmail === undefined`). The TypeScript copy is still `ownerFrozen` in owner.ts:46, which repoOwnerStale uses. The two copies agree today, but a change to one will not reach the other. Fix: export the SQL form from owner.ts next to ownerFrozen, so one module holds both forms.

createProposal reads agentFirstRepo before it takes the project row lock at line 101. If a first sync holds that lock while it inserts the project's first specclaw proposal, the create has already decided 'not agent-first'. It then waits for the lock and inserts a hand-made H-series proposal into a project that has just become agent-first. Fix: run the agent-first check after the `for update` on the project row.
findings.scenario: The first CI push for HRI and a create_proposal for HRI run at the same time. The create succeeds as HRI-H001 even though HRI is now agent-first.

findings.message: The rule counts any proposal with source 'specclaw' on the project, whichever repo brought it in. Unlinking keeps those rows. So a project relinked to a different repo is agent-first at once, and the refusal names the new repo, which has never synced. That contradicts the README line 'A freshly linked project keeps manual creation until its first sync.' Either tie the rule to a sync from the current repo_url (for example a delivery.sync_push row for that repo), or narrow the README and the 093 decision to say that relinking keeps the project agent-first.
findings.scenario: FLT is linked to repo A, a sync brings in FLT-701, and FLT is unlinked and then linked to repo B with no sync yet. create_proposal on FLT is refused with "FLT's proposals come from its repo (B)", although B has brought in nothing.
